title: Cassini meetings context v1
description: One or more recorded meetings rendered as context an agent can read: what the meeting was, who spoke, the transcript as speaker-attributed prose, and the generated summary when there is one. Produced by `cassini meetings context [--json]`. A document carrying one meeting is the bare meeting object; a document carrying several is a container whose every element is itself a complete, valid document of the first kind. That is the whole of the multi-meeting design: a reader written against a single meeting keeps working, because what it knows how to read is exactly what each element is. The markdown rendering of the same bundle is the same information for a human or a model to read directly, and is not described here.

meetings.description: The meetings, in the order the caller asked for them. Order is never reassigned by the producer: a caller that named three meetings gets them back in that order, which is what makes a bundle reproducible from its command line. A meeting the caller cannot read fails the whole run rather than shrinking this array — a bundle that quietly dropped one would answer a question asked of every meeting using only some of them. The producer collapses a one-meeting bundle to the bare meetingContext form instead of writing a one-element array here.

speakers.description: The roster declared by the recording, absent when it declares none.

transcriptSource.description: How the prose was produced, and load-bearing rather than decoration. An operator-published .opus carries raw-ASR word timings and nothing else — no readable transcript, no display transcript — so the prose in every bundle was assembled from those timings by the producer. A consumer must not present it as editorially cleaned-up text.

sourceTranscriptId.description: Id of the transcript inside the recording that the prose was derived from, so a claim can be traced back to the file.

segments.description: The transcript as speaker-attributed paragraphs, in chronological order. Always present: a meeting with no transcribed speech carries an empty array, which is a different fact from the field being absent.

id.description: The id the caller asked for, which is the id the published catalog indexes by. It is deliberately not the recording manifest's own meeting id: that one is content-derived, a hash of the audio, and cannot be used to correlate the bundle with the catalog entry it came from.

roomId.description: Id of the conversation this meeting was recorded in, shaped rm_<16 lowercase hex>. Absent when the room is unknown, which is an ordinary state for an import or a simulated run. Read from the catalog entry, falling back to the recording's own tag: the catalog is what a backfill and a reattribution keep current.

roomName.description: Display name of that conversation. Catalog-only, because a display name is editable and a sealed recording is not. Absent when the room is unknown, and absent for a meeting resolved without a catalog entry.

label.description: The speaker's display label, falling back to the raw id so an unlabelled speaker is still attributed rather than dropped.

segment.description: One paragraph of derived prose. The offsets are milliseconds from the start of the recording; the markdown rendering can cite startMs as MM:SS, or H:MM:SS past an hour. Both speaker fields are absent when the recording attributed nothing, which is not the same as one speaker who was never named.

present.description: Whether a summary was generated at all. Explicit so a consumer can tell "no summary was generated" from "the summary was empty": summaries are LLM-gated, and a deployment with no summariser configured publishes transcripts without them.

markdown.description: The summary exactly as it was authored, headings and all. The markdown rendering demotes those headings so they nest under its own "## Summary"; this field is never rewritten.
